exemplars.title: I Felt Bad After We Ignored Her: Understanding How Interface-Driven Social Prominence Shapes Group Discussions with GenAI
exemplars.why: The agent occupies a human seat at the roundtable and speaks from that position, making its rendered body both the locus of its turns and the mechanism that grants it social prominence in group discussion.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It edges out HAT Swapping because the evidence establishes both human-slot occupancy and embodied turn-taking, while the instructor stand-in quote establishes role substitution but not how outputs issue from the figure.

exemplars.title: HAT Swapping: Virtual Agents as Stand-Ins for Absent Human Instructors in Virtual Training
exemplars.why: The EVA appears in the absent instructor’s place and assumes the instructor’s guidance role, providing an unusually clean example of an agent body occupying a slot ordinarily held by a specific human participant.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above the simulated patient because literal substitution into an absent person’s position expresses the participant-slot signature more distinctly than a conventional embodied training character.

exemplars.title: Scaffolding Empathy: Training Counselors with Simulated Patients and Utterance-level Performance Visualizations
exemplars.why: The simulated patient receives typed input and emits synthesized speech and animated nonverbal behavior through an embodied conversational figure, clearly making that figure the perceptual source of the agent’s responses.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It displaces Future You because its evidence specifies the complete embodied interaction loop and animated output locus, whereas the future-self evidence names a talking avatar modality without establishing its interface position or behavior in comparable detail.

notes: I retained the first two consensus choices but selected consensus #4, rid 4423, instead of #3, rid 10283. Future You is conceptually distinctive and experimentally isolates embodiment, but its abstract-level evidence only names a photorealistic talking avatar; it does not clearly demonstrate the persistent positioned figure required by the structural signature. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should still treat persistence and exact on-screen extent as partly inferred for rid 12692 and rid 4423: their quotes establish an embodied role and expressive output but do not describe the full layout. Rid 5135 has the strongest structural evidence, although its figure caption likewise provides limited rendering detail.
